issue.title: sase memory read is dead on this host: home root collides between ~/sase/memory and legacy ~/memory, and the raw LayoutCollisionError offers no recovery
issue.description:
Every `sase memory read` on this host fails with an unhandled `LayoutCollisionError`
traceback, so the audited-read path that agent instructions make mandatory is
unavailable. The failure is not project-scoped: it comes from the *home* memory root,
so it breaks memory reads for every SASE project on the machine.

`resolve_memory_selector_batch` calls `_discover_link_universe`, which resolves the home
memory root via `memory_read_root` -> `CompatibleLayoutPath.resolve_read`. That helper
raises when both the canonical and the legacy candidate exist. On this host both do:

- canonical `~/sase/memory` (assets, obsidian.md, README.md, sase.md, sase_beads.md)
- legacy `~/memory` (assets, long/, short/, obsidian.md, README.md, sase.md)

`~/memory/{short,long}` is the pre-web layout, so the home tree looks like a
half-finished migration to the canonical root. The canonical root is the live one.

Two things are wrong and either would be worth fixing alone:

1. **No recovery path is offered.** The user sees a raw 12-frame traceback ending in
   "migrate to the canonical path instead of merging split state" with no command to
   run. A collision on the *home* root should be a diagnosed, actionable failure --
   ideally a `sase doctor` check plus a migration the user can run -- not an
   unhandled exception out of a read-only command.
2. **A home-root collision takes down project reads that do not need the home root at
   all.** Both selectors requested here (`tui_perf.md`, `lint_and_test.md`) exist in
   the project's own `sase/memory/`. The home root is consulted only to build the link
   universe, yet its collision fails the whole batch before anything is printed.

Impact is high for agents: `sase memory read` is the only sanctioned way to read
reference memory, and CLAUDE.md marks some of those reads mandatory
(`lint_and_test.md` "you MUST read this note before you finish your turn"). With this
broken, every agent on this machine must either skip a required read or work around it.
The workaround found while planning was to re-run under a fabricated `HOME` containing
only a symlinked `sase/memory`, which is not something an agent should have to invent.

task_type_fields.impact:
Blocks every SASE agent on this host from making any audited reference-memory read,
including the reads CLAUDE.md marks mandatory. Affects all projects on the machine, not
just sase, because the collision is on the home root.
task_type_fields.repro:
From any workspace on this host:

```
$ sase memory read tui_perf.md lint_and_test.md -r "any reason"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../sase/memory/selector.py", line 184, in resolve_memory_selector_batch
    link_notes, scoped_webs = _discover_link_universe(project_root, resolved_home_root)
  File ".../sase/memory/notes.py", line 323, in _iter_discoverable_memory_paths
    memory_root = source_memory_root or memory_read_root(root)
  File ".../sase/core/content_layout_wire.py", line 99, in resolve_read
    raise LayoutCollisionError(label, resolution.existing)
sase.core.content_layout_wire.LayoutCollisionError: memory exists in multiple
canonical/legacy locations: /Users/bbugyi/sase/memory, /Users/bbugyi/memory;
migrate to the canonical path instead of merging split state
```

`sase memory show` fails identically, as does any selector shape (flat note, bare web,
`web:keyword`), because the batch resolves before anything prints.

Reproduced 2026-09-01 from workspace sase_11 while planning unrelated Admin Center work.
Confirmed both roots exist with `ls -la /Users/bbugyi/memory /Users/bbugyi/sase/memory`.

payload.description: Both are home-root memory defects: sase-vu writes regenerated home memory to the wrong chezmoi checkout; sase-vz is a home root split across ~/sase/memory and legacy ~/memory.
